body:
A dry hit is one of the most unpleasant experiences in vaping: a sharp, harsh, burnt draw, sometimes with no vapor at all, that makes you cough and wince. It happens when the coil heats cotton instead of liquid, and it is almost always preventable. This guide explains what a dry hit is, why it happens, how to recognize one, what to do right after, how to fix the underlying cause, how to prevent it in pods, tanks and disposables, how liquid thickness, power, priming and puffing habits matter, how to tell a dry hit from other problems and when to replace the coil. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice. If you feel unwell after a dry hit, stop using the device, drink water and seek advice if symptoms continue.

## What a dry hit is
A dry hit occurs when the wick does not hold enough liquid when the coil fires. Without liquid to absorb the heat, the cotton itself heats, scorches and produces acrid, burnt-tasting vapor. The coil is hotter than intended, and the draw is harsh. The effect lasts a moment, but the damage to the wick can last, and a burnt wick keeps tasting burnt even when it is wet again.

## Why it happens
### Low liquid
If the tank or pod runs low, the wick is no longer fully covered. Refill before it is nearly empty.

### An unprimed coil
A new coil with dry cotton fired at once is the most common cause. Priming prevents it. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).

### Chain vaping
Rapid puffs use liquid faster than the wick can draw it in, so the coil runs dry. Take breaks.

### Too much power
Running above the coil's range heats it faster than liquid can supply. Lower the power.

### Liquid too thick for the coil
High-VG liquid wicks slowly. In a small coil or pod, it cannot keep up, so the wick dries. Match liquid to hardware; see [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/).

### Airflow problems
Too tight an airflow can overheat the coil, and blocked wicking holes can starve the cotton. Check them.

### A worn coil
A clogged coil wicks poorly. Replace it. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/).

### Tilting or lying the device flat
If the tank is on its side, the coil may not be in contact with liquid. Keep it upright.

## How to recognize a dry hit
- A sudden harsh, burnt, acrid taste.
- Little or no vapor, or hot, dry vapor.
- A scratchy throat and coughing.
- A faint burnt smell.
- A coil that sizzles or crackles.

If you notice these, stop at once.

## What to do right after
1. Stop vaping, and put the device down.
2. Drink some water and breathe normally.
3. Check the liquid level, and refill if low.
4. Let the coil rest for several minutes, so that the wick soaks.
5. Take a gentle puff to test.
6. If it still tastes burnt, the wick may be damaged. Replace the coil or pod.

Do not keep puffing to see whether it clears, because that only burns more cotton.

## Preventing dry hits
- **Prime every new coil.**
- **Keep liquid above the minimum.**
- **Take steady puffs with breaks.**
- **Use suitable liquid** for the coil.
- **Keep power in range.**
- **Replace coils on time.**
- **Store devices upright.**

## Dry hits in different devices
### Disposables
A dry hit late in a disposable's life usually means liquid is nearly gone. Heavy chain vaping can also cause one earlier. If it happens, rest the device, and replace it if it persists. You cannot refill or repair a disposable.

### Pods
Check that the pod has liquid, and that it is seated properly. Replace a worn pod. Refillable pods need a soak after filling.

### Tanks
Check the liquid level and the coil. Prime a new coil thoroughly, and match power and airflow.

## How to tell a dry hit from other problems
A dry hit gives a harsh, burnt draw. A flooded coil gives gurgling and wet vapor. A low battery gives weak, cool vapor. A worn coil gives flat flavor. A blocked airflow gives a tight, hard draw. Knowing the difference helps you fix the right thing. See [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/) and [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/).

## A worked example
You pick up your tank after a few hours and take a long drag. It tastes burnt, and you cough. You check the window and see the liquid is below the wicking holes. You refill, wait ten minutes and take a gentle puff. It tastes fine, and the coil seems fine. Had you taken several more hard puffs on the dry coil, it would have been ruined. The fix cost you nothing but a few minutes, because you stopped and checked.

## When to replace the coil
If a burnt taste persists after resting and refilling, the cotton is probably scorched. Replace the coil or pod, and prime the new one. Keep a spare. A scorched coil will not recover, and continuing to use it is unpleasant.

## Habits that help
Check the liquid level before you start vaping each day. Refill when the level is about half. Prime new coils. Take a short break every few puffs. Use the recommended liquid and power. Store the device upright. These small habits prevent nearly every dry hit.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Is a dry hit harmful?
We make no health claims. It is unpleasant and a sign that the device is not working as intended. Stop using it and fix the cause.

### Can a dry hit damage my device?
It can damage the coil and wick. The battery is usually fine.

### Why do I get dry hits only at certain times?
Often when liquid is low, or after a period of chain vaping. Check your habits.

### Can thick liquid cause dry hits in a new coil?
Yes. High-VG liquid soaks slowly, so prime for longer.

### What if I get dry hits from a new pod?
It may not have soaked. Rest it, and use gentle puffs. If it persists, contact us if it is from us.

## Shop
Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A closer look at wicking
Wicking is how liquid travels through cotton to the coil. It depends on the cotton's density, the liquid's thickness and the coil's design. Thin liquid wicks fast, thick liquid slowly. A coil with large wicking holes feeds liquid quickly, and one with small holes needs thinner liquid. If wicking cannot keep up with your puffs, the cotton dries, and you get a dry hit. This is why matching liquid, coil and power matters, and why slower, steadier puffs help. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/) and [what is a mesh coil](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/).

## Case studies
### The long draw
A customer took long, hard puffs on a small pod and got repeated dry hits. Shorter, gentler puffs, with a brief pause between, stopped them. Lesson: puff style matters.

### The thick liquid
A customer used a 70 percent VG liquid in a pod designed for 50/50. Dry hits were frequent. Switching to the recommended liquid solved it. Lesson: use the liquid the device is made for.

### The empty tank
A customer left a tank nearly empty overnight, then took a puff in the morning. A dry hit. Refilling and resting fixed it. Lesson: check the level before the first puff.

## Building a pre-puff habit
Before you vape, glance at the liquid level, and make sure the device is upright and charged. After you refill, rest it. Take your first puff gently. It takes a second, and it prevents most dry hits. Habits like these cost nothing, and they protect your coils and your throat.

## What not to do after a dry hit
Do not increase the power to "clear" the taste. Do not keep puffing until the taste fades. Do not rinse the coil. Do not ignore it. Stop, rest and check, then replace if needed.

## Frequently asked questions about dry hits
### Can a dry hit happen with a full tank?
Yes, if the coil is unprimed, worn or fed by liquid that is too thick, or if you chain vape. A full tank does not guarantee a wet wick.

### Why does it happen more on a new device?
New coils need priming. Skipping it is the most common reason.

### How do I tell a dry hit from a leak?
A dry hit is harsh and burnt. A leak is wet and messy. They have opposite causes.

### Should I replace a coil after one dry hit?
Not always. If it recovers after resting and tastes right, it may be fine. If the burnt taste persists, replace it.

### Can I prevent dry hits with settings?
Moderate power, suitable airflow and steady puffs help a great deal.

### One more habit worth building
Keep a spare primed coil or pod within reach, so that if a dry hit damages the one in use, you can swap at once, and carry on without waiting for an order.
